first.rationale: The most urgent and directly addressable threat to sustainable long-term qualified revenue is the competitor's aggressive entry pricing pulling price-sensitive SMB accounts away. memory_73 is the most relevant inherited evidence, claiming promotional pricing works well for exactly this segment, with compounding benefits (acquisition, revenue, time-to-value, cross-plan consistency). Because the claim is unusually broad and stacks several benefits that could mask a discounting/margin-erosion risk to 'qualified' (i.e., high-LTV) revenue, I want to verify the original record before committing spend. Activation and onboarding declines are real but slower-moving and already have two corroborating archived memories (31, 86) suggesting a known lever exists if needed later; the competitive pricing threat is time-sensitive and only one slot exists this week, so it takes priority. I'm not verifying a second memory since the pricing decision hinges primarily on 73's fidelity, and spending the second verification wouldn't change this week's action. Given uncertainty about whether discount-driven acquisition holds up as genuinely qualified, durable revenue (versus short-term volume that could undercut brand/price positioning), I'm sizing this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with explicit tracking of downstream retention/quality metrics, not just week-one lift.
